findings.finding: The superseding AC list's final criterion 'No behaviour change to any script invoked by .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml' names no proving method, whereas the original list specified 'verified by a CI run, not inspection'. As written, the superseding criterion could be satisfied by inspection alone.
findings.location: AC (supersedes) — final bullet 'No behaviour change to any script invoked by _build-and-test.yml'
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the final superseding AC to read: 'The seven CI-invoked gate scripts behave identically, verified by a green .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml run — not inspection.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether any of the 12 pre-existing dead RUF100 directives are noqa:T201 sites already inside the 28-directive set, so the two deletion counts are reconciled and non-overlapping (or explicitly overlapping).
evidence: 'The 28 substantive pre-existing ruff check violations are resolved (RUF100 x12, ...)'
'Measured on the current tree: 28 inline # noqa: T201 directives across 13 files'
The RUF100 x12 was 'measured against the PRE-consolidation config' per CORRECTION 2, so some of those 12 dead directives may themselves be noqa:T201 sites
findings.finding: The number '28' names two distinct sets without clarifying their overlap: the '28 substantive pre-existing ruff check violations (RUF100 x12, E501 x11, ...)' and the '28 inline noqa:T201 directives' that become redundant after consolidation. An executor cannot tell whether any of the 12 pre-existing RUF100 dead directives are ALREADY among the 28 T201 directives (a currently-unused noqa:T201 would be counted in both), risking double-counting or missed deletions.
findings.location: CORRECTION 2 + final Acceptance Criteria (RUF100 x12 vs 28 inline noqa:T201)
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence reconciling the sets, e.g. 'Of the 28 noqa:T201 directives, N are already dead pre-consolidation (part of the RUF100 x12); the remaining M become dead on consolidation — all 28 are deleted in the same change.'

findings.finding: The plan's prose states 'seven of these files are invoked directly by .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml' and enumerates seven, but the workflow invokes at least eleven scripts/ files — it also calls gen_cli_reference.py, gen_mcp_reference.py, check_server_manifest.py, and check_config_reads.py. The blast-radius claim and the (later-superseded) AC 'the seven CI-invoked gate scripts behave identically' are built on an incomplete list.

scenarios: Reviewer relies on the 'seven' list to scope the CI-parity verification and skips checking gen_cli_reference.py / gen_mcp_reference.py / check_server_manifest.py / check_config_reads.py output after reformatting
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'seven' with the full list of scripts invoked by _build-and-test.yml (add gen_cli_reference.py:471, gen_mcp_reference.py:491, check_server_manifest.py:535, check_config_reads.py:566) so the blast-radius and parity AC cover all CI-invoked gate scripts.

findings.finding: The plan edits scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py (the two RUF059 fixes) and reformats scripts/ wholesale, but does not enumerate that file's consumers outside scripts/: it is invoked by a SEPARATE workflow .github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml, imported by file-path in tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py and tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py, and cross-imports jira_dc_field_readiness (also in the reformat scope). findings.location: Section 'The 50 T201 (print) violations' + AC 'RUF100 x12' / 'consolidated per-file-ignores entry'
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run `ruff check scripts/` with the proposed `"scripts/**" = ["T201"]` entry applied to get the TRUE post-consolidation RUF100 count, then have the plan delete all now-redundant inline `# noqa: T201` sites (ruff --fix handles this) as part of the RUF100 acceptance criterion.
